sources.support: Provenance: imper.ai reports observations made during its own pre-employment verification work for an unnamed global enterprise. The live site blocked unauthenticated retrieval during this pass; the exact first-party page was recovered from an Internet Archive capture dated 2026-05-11. imper.ai says it screened 600 candidates in Q1 2026 and identified four with overlapping device, network, remote-access, location-consistency, VoIP, and low-history account signals that it assessed as consistent with published DPRK IT-worker tradecraft. It rates attribution moderate-to-high and expressly does not claim definitive attribution without more corroboration. Normalized boundary: imper.ai assessed four of 600 screened candidates in Q1 2026 as exhibiting a correlated set of indicators consistent with DPRK IT-worker tradecraft. Attribution boundary: Vendor assessment of four applicants for one unnamed customer; no government finding, legal identity, hire, or post-hire access is established. Publication boundary: Retain only the aggregate 600-screened/four-flagged applicant finding and the source's own attribution caveat. Do not publish candidate selectors or treat VPN, latency, remote-access software, VoIP, or account age alone as determinative
